title: June 2026 Feature Updates: /cd Command and Auto Mode Improvements
description: Claude Code released multiple updates in early-mid June 2026, including the /cd command (June 8-12) to move sessions to new working directories mid-conversation without rebuilding prompts, and auto mode safety improvements on Bedrock, Vertex, and other platforms (June 19, version 2.1.170).

community_feedback.quote: Those Claude Code hacks are crazy! Tons of things I'm using and things I don't even know.
Founders report code quality from Claude Code was as good or better than their engineers, with reduced turnaround time.

title: June 15 Billing Change: Agent SDK and Headless Usage Moved to Separate Credits
description: On June 15, 2026, Anthropic moved Claude Agent SDK, headless Claude Code, Claude Code GitHub Actions, and third-party agents to separate credit-based billing. Pro plans get $20 in API credits, Max 5x gets $100, with per-user credits ranging from $20-$200 replacing flat-rate access.

community_feedback.quote: Claude took the unfair bullet - agentic software doesn't fit seat-based pricing models

title: June 18, 2026: /automate Skill and GitHub/Slack Triggers
description: Cursor released a major update on June 18, 2026, introducing the /automate skill that lets AI agents set up automations for users in plain language. The release also included new triggers for GitHub and Slack integrations, alongside general improvements to Cursor automations.

community_feedback.quote: Cursor just launched /automate - a skill that lets agents set up automations for you in plain language. Describe the task.

title: June 17, 2026: Automations 3.7 with Enhanced BugBot
description: On June 17, 2026, Cursor released Automations 3.7 with cloud improvements and significantly enhanced BugBot - now over 3x faster, 22% cheaper, and finding 10% more bugs. The release also introduced new Design Mode features.

title: June 1, 2026: Major Billing Overhaul - Usage-Based Credits Replace Request-Based Billing
description: Starting June 1, 2026, GitHub moved Copilot from request-based billing (Premium Request Units) to usage-based billing using GitHub AI Credits based on token consumption. Copilot Business: $19/user/month with 1,900 AI Credits. Copilot Enterprise: $39/user/month. Code review now consumes both GitHub Actions minutes and AI Credits.

community_feedback.quote: What a joke - GitHub Copilot's new token-based billing spurs consternation among devs
Users fear they can no longer budget fixed monthly costs and worry about unpredictable bills

title: June 18, 2026: Google Discontinues Gemini CLI for All User Tiers
description: On June 18, 2026, Google shut down Gemini CLI for free, Pro, and Ultra users. The 105,000-star open-source coding tool was replaced with 'Antigravity CLI'. The shutdown caused CI/CD pipeline disruptions and forced developers to migrate to alternatives.

community_feedback.quote: Reports of pipelines breaking as the shutdown took effect
Concerns about losing terminal-based AI capabilities

title: June 17, 2026: Enterprise Admin Enforcement for Automations
description: On June 17, 2026, Devin added the ability for enterprise admins to enforce automations and service users to fall back to the Devin identity across all organizations. Additionally, all Devin reviews now include a security discovery section that follows the repository's SECURITY.md file.

title: June 2026: Goal Mode Goes Stable with GPT-5.5
description: In June 2026, OpenAI's Codex CLI marked Goal mode as stable after experimental period. The feature, now integrated with GPT-5.5, is described as 'the autonomy champion' capable of running for hours without supervision. Users report leaving it running for 18 hours where it 'shipped 14 of 18 features solo'. GPT-5.5 scores 82.7% on Terminal-Bench 2.0.

community_feedback.quote: Goal mode is the autonomy champion - can run for hours without supervision. Shipped 14 of 18 features solo in 18 hours
GPT 5.5-med causes the most regressions and coding issues
Concerns about OpenAI lock-in with the new recommended model setup
